html:
Saudi Vision 2030 is a plan announced in April 2016 by Mohammed bin Salman, then deputy crown prince, to make Saudi Arabia less dependent on oil by 2030.

It aimed to grow tourism, mining, entertainment and private business, and to bring more women into work. A small share of Saudi Aramco was sold on the stock market in 2019, and the state wealth fund put money into giant projects such as NEOM, a planned city on the Red Sea. Cinemas reopened, concerts were allowed and women were allowed to drive in 2018.

At the same time dissent was crushed, and the murder of the journalist Jamal Khashoggi in 2018 damaged the crown prince abroad. Some of the giant projects were scaled back. See also Saudi Arabia.
sum: Saudi Vision 2030 is a plan announced in April 2016 by Mohammed bin Salman, then deputy crown prince, to make Saudi Arabia less dependent on oil by 2030.
